title_or_table: Housing Vacancies and Homeownership, Annual Statistics: 2003, Table B-7, Standard Errors for Homeownership Rate by Race of Householder; Annual Statistics: 2025, Table B-7, Margins of Error for Homeownership Rates, by Race and Ethnicity
universe_or_base: Households by race and ethnicity of householder: non-Hispanic White, Black and Hispanic
unit: percent and percentage points; 2003 standard errors are published (68 chances in 100), 2025 margins are published at 90 percent; gaps and changes computed by the studio with s = sqrt(s1 squared plus s2 squared)
vintage: 2003 annual statistics as posted; 2025 annual statistics dated March 24, 2026
qualification: Published errors are rounded to one decimal, so the computed margins are approximate. The 2003 table labels its Black row "Black, total"; Table 22 of the 2025 release gives the same 48.1 for 2003 as race alone. The non-Hispanic White and Black gap widened by 2.3 points from 2003 to 2025, and the non-Hispanic White and Hispanic gap narrowed by 2.9 points; each change passes its margin of about 0.7 points (DR-64)

value.description: homeownership rate, or the gap in points

printed_source_line: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, Housing Vacancies and Homeownership, Annual Statistics 2003 and 2025, Table B-7, standard errors and margins of error of homeownership rates by race and ethnicity, 2003 and 2025, United States. Retrieved November 11, 2026. Margins of the gaps computed by Oath & Action.
